A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciAgentGym study. All 33 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, equations, figures, tables, and case studies, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, SciAgent fine-tuning results, training ablations, scaling experiments, and failure analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised numerical results in Tables 3 and 4.

M1.justification: The tool environment, dependency-graph sampling, execution verification, error-recovery trajectories, question generation, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 clarifies filesystem permissions, consistent with artifact-writing functionality already documented in v1; it does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 259 tasks and 1,134 sub-questions across the same four scientific domains, multimodal and unimodal coverage, and three difficulty levels. Training-data coverage and case-study scenarios are unchanged. Corrected source citations do not establish changed datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same evaluated model families and comparison variants, including tool-free baselines and OtherTools, NoError, single-domain, and merged-data variants. Citation corrections do not add or remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4 revises the stated SPL reference from an expert-verified shortest path to an expert-verified reference path, aligning it with Appendix C.2. The formula and detailed evaluation settings remain unchanged. Appendix A's effective-evaluated-set note is additional disclosure, not evidence that sample selection or experiments changed.

E4.justification: The ablation questions and configurations, data-scaling experiment, feedback and recovery analyses, and Appendix F case studies are retained. Table 4's numerical revisions change reported results, but no ablation or supplementary analysis is added, removed, or redesigned.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly states that unresolved non-response cases remained after repeated reruns. This adds qualitative run-reporting information beyond the retained retry safeguards; it does not establish increased replication. No new run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises the central difficulty breakdown and some rankings. GPT-5's L1/L2/L3 scores change from 60.6/38.6/30.9 to 58.8/38.4/34.6; SciAgent-4B's L1 advantage over its base reverses from +2.6 to -2.3 points. Aggregate rows and Table 4 ablation scores also change, including the base score from 23.0 to 23.4 and Merged from 30.0 to 30.1. Overall per-model benchmark scores remain unchanged. These are revised reported results, not demonstrated performance gains from a changed method.

T1.justification: The definition of SPL's reference length drops the shortest-path qualification, removing an optimality assumption inconsistent with the existing Appendix C.2 caveat. This is a limited mathematical-definition correction; the equations, dependency-graph formalism, and Algorithm 1 otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain: SciAgentGym and SciAgentBench support scientific tool-use evaluation, long-horizon tasks remain difficult, and SciForge training improves small models and supports cross-domain transfer. The abstract removes specific GPT-5 percentages, while the introduction updates them without changing the overarching claim.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 replaces steadily improving performance with improvement despite non-monotonic fluctuations, matching the unchanged Figure 5. Section 4 also removes the shortest-path characterization, bringing the main text into agreement with the existing SPL limitation. The principal failure-mechanism and transfer interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3 clarifies read-only problem assets versus a writable working directory. Appendix A newly explains that success rates use model- and subset-specific effective evaluated sets after unresolved non-responses, without supplying their sizes. Conversely, v2 removes the only code-and-data release statement and repository link. Training hyperparameters and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the distinct R-Bench reference and corrects the main-text R-Bench-V citation to the already-listed RBench-V work; it also fixes the ScienceQA attribution. Other bibliography changes largely update metadata or publication venues. The related-work comparisons and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, several explanatory sentences are refined, and the date and bibliography are updated. The section sequence and Appendix A–F organization remain intact, with no extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 5 relabels its aggregate columns from Avg to Overall. Table 4 has modest width, wrapping, and caption-layout adjustments, accompanied by local page reflow. All figures and tables are retained; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves concrete inconsistencies: Table 3 aggregates now agree with Table 5, and Table 4's base and Merged scores agree with Table 3. Its SPL wording and scaling interpretation also better match existing evidence. Removing the sole repository link weakens access documentation, and effective sample sizes remain unspecified, but the gains in numerical consistency and interpretive accuracy support a limited overall improvement.
